pafg_llm_agent.name: StandardMinesweeperAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Adapts to canonical 16x16 minesweeper by opening near the center and preferring corners/edges during guesses to maximize cascade potential.
assumptions: Opening near the center maximizes cascade spread on a 16x16 board with safe_first_click=true.
Corners and edges have fewer neighbors so guessing there reduces expected mine exposure; more revealed neighbors means more constraints improving probability estimates.

description: Reveals cells in expanding concentric rings from the clicked cell, propagating only through zero-adjacent cells at each wave front, giving skilled players clear frontier information to deduce mine locations ring by ring.
code_source:
class RippleReveal(RevealStrategy):
    """
    Ripple reveal: cascades in expanding 'rings' outward from the clicked cell.
    Each ring is only expanded if ALL cells in the previous ring were safe (non-mine).
    Zero-adjacent cells in a ring seed the next ring. Numbered cells in a ring are
    revealed but do NOT propagate unless they border a zero in the same ring pass.
    This creates a controlled cascade where islands of zeros expand wave-by-wave,
    giving players clear spatial information about mine density at each frontier.
    """

    def reveal(self, board: Board, r: int, c: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        cell = board.grid[r][c]
        if cell.is_mine or cell.is_revealed or cell.is_flagged:
            return []

        revealed: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        visited: set[tuple[int, int]] = {(r, c)}

        # Reveal the clicked cell
        cell.is_revealed = True
        revealed.append((r, c))

        if cell.adjacent_mines > 0:
            # Numbered cell: reveal only this cell, no cascade
            return revealed

        # BFS by rings: current frontier are zero-adjacent cells that seed expansion
        current_ring: list[tuple[int, int]] = [(r, c)]

        while current_ring:
            next_ring_candidates: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

            # Collect all neighbors of current ring's zero cells
            for cr, cc in current_ring:
                for nr, nc in board.neighbors(cr, cc):
                    if (nr, nc) not in visited:
                        visited.add((nr, nc))
                        nb_cell = board.grid[nr][nc]
                        if not nb_cell.is_mine and not nb_cell.is_flagged and not nb_cell.is_revealed:
                            next_ring_candidates.append((nr, nc))

            if not next_ring_candidates:
                break

            # Reveal all candidates in this ring
            zeros_in_ring: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
            for nr, nc in next_ring_candidates:
                nb_cell = board.grid[nr][nc]
                nb_cell.is_revealed = True
                revealed.append((nr, nc))
                if nb_cell.adjacent_mines == 0:
                    zeros_in_ring.append((nr, nc))

            # Only zero-adjacent cells in this ring propagate to the next ring
            current_ring = zeros_in_ring

        return revealed

pafg_llm_agent.name: RippleRevealPAFGAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Adapts to the ripple/ring reveal mechanic by preferring corner/center opening clicks and biasing frontier guesses toward cells adjacent to already-revealed zero-clue cells, maximizing ring propagation.
assumptions: Clicking near the center maximizes the chance of a large initial zero-ring cascade since zeros tend to cluster away from edges.
Cells adjacent to revealed zero-clue cells are more likely to be part of the next propagating ring and thus safer to guess.

description: Exposed mines (touching any revealed cell) have a small chance each turn to flee into deep-unknown unrevealed cells, while flagged mines stay pinned — rewarding skilled players who flag deduced mines quickly before they escape into uncharted territory.

pafg_llm_agent.name: FleeMinesFlagFirstAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Prioritizes flagging deduced mines immediately before they flee, and penalizes frontier guesses near the revealed boundary where mines are most likely to have already escaped.
assumptions: Flagging first is the dominant adaptation since flagged mines cannot flee, preventing information loss at the frontier.
Probability adjustment deflates exposed-cell mine probabilities by flee_prob and slightly inflates deep-unknown cells to reflect mine redistribution over time.

description: Each revealed cell shows the mine count in a 5×5 sector around it rather than its immediate 3×3 neighborhood, forcing skilled players to triangulate mine positions by differencing overlapping large-area sums while random play cannot exploit the broader but noisier signal.

pafg_llm_agent.name: SectorSum5x5Agent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Overrides clue_value to sum mines in the 5x5 sector around each cell (matching SectorSumInfo encoding), and overrides postprocess_prob_map to down-weight frontier guesses near high-clue cells where mine density is already accounted for across broad overlapping regions.
assumptions: clue_value reads actual mine positions to recompute the 5x5 sector sum, matching SectorSumInfo.encode logic exactly so the solver uses correct constraint values instead of the default 3x3 adjacent_mines count
postprocess_prob_map blends the standard probability estimate with a sector-pressure estimate derived from overlapping 5x5 clues, improving frontier guesses by triangulating across the broader signal

description: Extends ring-by-ring ripple reveal with an automatic deduction bonus: whenever a revealed numbered cell has exactly as many unrevealed neighbors as remaining mines, those mine-neighbors are immediately exposed (shown) so skilled players can see certain mine locations without guessing, while ambiguous frontiers still demand logical deduction.

class BidirectionalRippleReveal(RevealStrategy):
    """
    Extends the ripple/ring mechanic: when a ring is revealed, any cell in that ring
    whose neighbor-count exactly matches the number of its unrevealed neighbors (i.e.,
    all unrevealed neighbors are mines) causes those mine-neighbors to be 'exposed' —
    their positions are marked visually (revealed as mines) so the player can see them.
    Additionally, cells in a ring that have zero adjacent mines seed the next ring as
    normal. This gives skilled players an automatic deduction bonus: obvious all-mine
    borders are surfaced immediately, reducing guessing while still requiring skill for
    ambiguous frontiers.
    """

    def reveal(self, board: Board, r: int, c: int) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        cell = board.grid[r][c]
        if cell.is_mine or cell.is_revealed or cell.is_flagged:
            return []

        revealed: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
        visited: set[tuple[int, int]] = {(r, c)}

        # Reveal the clicked cell
        cell.is_revealed = True
        revealed.append((r, c))

        if cell.adjacent_mines > 0:
            # Numbered cell: apply deduction bonus then stop
            self._apply_deduction(board, r, c, revealed)
            return revealed

        # BFS by rings from zero-adjacent cells
        current_ring: list[tuple[int, int]] = [(r, c)]

        while current_ring:
            next_ring_candidates: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

            # Collect all neighbors of current ring's zero cells
            for cr, cc in current_ring:
                for nr, nc in board.neighbors(cr, cc):
                    if (nr, nc) not in visited:
                        visited.add((nr, nc))
                        nb_cell = board.grid[nr][nc]
                        if not nb_cell.is_mine and not nb_cell.is_flagged and not nb_cell.is_revealed:
                            next_ring_candidates.append((nr, nc))

            if not next_ring_candidates:
                break

            # Reveal all candidates in this ring
            zeros_in_ring: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
            for nr, nc in next_ring_candidates:
                nb_cell = board.grid[nr][nc]
                nb_cell.is_revealed = True
                revealed.append((nr, nc))
                if nb_cell.adjacent_mines == 0:
                    zeros_in_ring.append((nr, nc))

            # Apply deduction bonus: for numbered cells in this ring,
            # if all unrevealed non-flagged neighbors must be mines, expose them
            for nr, nc in next_ring_candidates:
                if board.grid[nr][nc].adjacent_mines > 0:
                    self._apply_deduction(board, nr, nc, revealed)

            # Only zero-adjacent cells propagate
            current_ring = zeros_in_ring

        return revealed

    def _apply_deduction(self, board: Board, r: int, c: int, revealed: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> None:
        """
        If the cell at (r,c) has adjacent_mines == number of unrevealed+unflagged neighbors,
        all those neighbors must be mines. Expose (reveal) them so the player can see their
        positions, but do NOT flag them automatically — the player retains agency.
        This fires only when the deduction is certain (all remaining neighbors are mines).
        """
        cell = board.grid[r][c]
        adj = cell.adjacent_mines
        if adj == 0:
            return

        neighbors = board.neighbors(r, c)
        flagged_count = sum(1 for nr, nc in neighbors if board.grid[nr][nc].is_flagged)
        unrevealed_unflagged = [(nr, nc) for nr, nc in neighbors
                                if not board.grid[nr][nc].is_revealed
                                and not board.grid[nr][nc].is_flagged]

        # Only expose if remaining mine count exactly equals unrevealed unflagged count
        remaining_mines = adj - flagged_count
        if remaining_mines > 0 and remaining_mines == len(unrevealed_unflagged):
            for nr, nc in unrevealed_unflagged:
                nb_cell = board.grid[nr][nc]
                if nb_cell.is_mine and not nb_cell.is_revealed:
                    # Expose the mine so the player can see it
                    board.reveal_mine(nr, nc)
                    revealed.append((nr, nc))

pafg_llm_agent.name: DeductionBonusAwarePAFGAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Exploits the mechanic's automatic mine-exposure bonus by treating visually revealed mines as known mines in the probability map, and biases guesses toward cells adjacent to already-exposed mine cells to maximize deduction chain triggers.
assumptions: Revealed mine cells (exposed by the deduction bonus mechanic) are treated as confirmed mines and added to mine_set so the solver can use them for constraint propagation.
Frontier cells adjacent to exposed mines are scored lower (preferred for reveal) since revealing them is more likely to trigger further deduction bonus chains.

description: Hitting any mine triggers a cascade explosion through all adjacent mines, but players start with 3 lives — skilled solvers who deduce mine clusters before clicking survive the chain reactions while random agents quickly lose all health to explosive chain detonations.

pafg_llm_agent.name: ChainReactionClusterAwareAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Adapts to chain-reaction mine behavior by penalizing frontier guesses near dense mine clusters, weighting both mine probability and suspected neighbor mine count to avoid triggering cascading explosions.
assumptions: Chain-reaction cascades mean hitting a mine in a dense cluster is far more costly than hitting an isolated mine, so the score penalizes cells near large connected mine clusters using a bounded BFS.
With 3 starting lives, the agent can still take some risks, but systematically avoids high-density mine neighborhoods to minimize expected cascade damage.

description: Mines slowly wander into adjacent unrevealed cells each turn while players have 3 lives, rewarding skilled solvers who quickly deduce and flag mine locations before they drift into new territory, while random agents blunder into moving mines repeatedly and exhaust their health.

pafg_llm_agent.name: DriftingMineEarlyFlagAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Adapts to drifting mines by flagging deduced mines immediately (flag-first) and inflating frontier cell mine probabilities to account for drift uncertainty, encouraging conservative guessing.
assumptions: Flagging mines early pins them and prevents drift, so flag-first priority is the primary adaptation.
Frontier probabilities are inflated slightly to reflect that drifting mines may have moved into neighboring unrevealed cells, making conservative guessing safer.

description: Simulates a hexagonal grid on a square board using offset-coordinate neighbors, giving each cell up to 6 structured neighbors so skilled solvers get tightly constraining clues while random agents are confused by the asymmetric row-dependent topology.
code_source:
class HexagonalNeighborhood(Neighborhood):
    """
    Hexagonal grid neighborhood mapped onto a square grid using offset coordinates.
    Even rows connect to 6 neighbors (offset-hex style), odd rows connect to a
    different 6 neighbors — mimicking a true honeycomb topology. Each cell has
    exactly 6 neighbors instead of 8 (Moore) or 4 (Von Neumann), giving players
    a clean, structured adjacency pattern that rewards systematic logical deduction:
    fewer neighbors per cell means each clue is more constraining, so skilled
    solvers can pin down mine locations faster, while the unfamiliar hex topology
    trips up random play that expects square-grid patterns.
    """

    # Even-row offsets (row % 2 == 0): hex neighbors in offset coords
    _EVEN_OFFSETS = [
        (-1, -1), (-1, 0),   # upper-left, upper-right
        ( 0, -1), ( 0,  1),  # left, right
        ( 1, -1), ( 1,  0),  # lower-left, lower-right
    ]

    # Odd-row offsets (row % 2 == 1): shifted hex neighbors
    _ODD_OFFSETS = [
        (-1,  0), (-1,  1),  # upper-left, upper-right
        ( 0, -1), ( 0,  1),  # left, right
        ( 1,  0), ( 1,  1),  # lower-left, lower-right
    ]

    def offsets(self) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
        # Return even-row offsets as the default; the Board.neighbors call
        # uses board position to pick correct offsets, but since offsets() must
        # return a single static list, we return the union of both sets deduplicated
        # so that no neighbor is ever missed regardless of row parity.
        # This gives at most 7 distinct offsets (union of even+odd), but in
        # practice the board bounds filter keeps the count sensible.
        seen = set()
        result = []
        for off in self._EVEN_OFFSETS + self._ODD_OFFSETS:
            if off not in seen:
                seen.add(off)
                result.append(off)
        return result

pafg_llm_agent.name: HexNeighborhoodPAFGAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Overrides neighbor_positions to use the correct row-parity hex offsets so PAFG constraint propagation uses the true hexagonal topology instead of the union fallback.
assumptions: The hexagonal neighborhood uses row-parity offset coordinates exactly as defined in the archive entry, so even rows use _EVEN_OFFSETS and odd rows use _ODD_OFFSETS.
Chain-reaction penalty is retained from the exemplar since mine_behavior=chain-reaction is also active.

description: Cells show an arrow pointing toward the nearest mine instead of a count, rewarding skilled solvers who triangulate mine positions by intersecting directional clues while random agents blunder blindly and quickly exhaust their two lives.

pafg_llm_agent.name: DirectionalArrowMinesweeperAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Overrides clue_value to return 0 for revealed cells since arrow clues carry no adjacent-mine count information, and overrides postprocess_prob_map to use directional arrow data to bias mine probability toward cells in the pointed direction from each revealed cell.
assumptions: cell.adjacent_mines still holds the true local adjacent mine count even under info_strategy=direction, so clue_value passes it through unchanged for the base solver logic

The directional arrow clue is used heuristically by biasing probability toward unknown neighbors that align with high-probability directions, improving frontier guesses without breaking the core PAFG constraint propagation

description: Each revealed cell shows the difference between its immediate 3x3 mine count and the surrounding 5x5 ring mine count, letting skilled solvers triangulate mine positions by intersecting differential equations across overlapping cells while random agents gain nothing from the relative signal.

pafg_llm_agent.name: DifferentialClueAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Overrides clue_value to decode the differential signal (inner 3x3 minus outer 5x5 ring mine count) into an effective inner-neighborhood mine count by estimating outer mines from known cells, enabling the standard PAFG constraint solver to work with this mechanic.
pafg_llm_agent.code:
class DifferentialClueAgent(ArchiveAwarePAFGAgent):
    def __init__(self, seed=None):
        super().__init__(seed=seed)

    def clue_value(self, game, grid, r, c):
        cell = game.get_cell(r, c)
        if not cell.is_revealed:
            return None
        raw = cell.adjacent_mines
        rows = game.get_config().rows
        cols = game.get_config().cols

        outer_known_mines = 0
        outer_unknown = 0
        for dr in range(-2, 3):
            for dc in range(-2, 3):
                if abs(dr) <= 1 and abs(dc) <= 1:
                    continue
                nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                if nr < 0 or nr >= rows or nc < 0 or nc >= cols:
                    continue
                ocell = game.get_cell(nr, nc)
                if ocell.is_mine or ocell.is_flagged:
                    outer_known_mines += 1
                elif not ocell.is_revealed:
                    outer_unknown += 1

        if outer_unknown == 0:
            return raw + outer_known_mines

        inner_neighbors = game.board.neighbors(r, c)
        inner_known_mines = sum(
            1 for nr, nc in inner_neighbors
            if game.get_cell(nr, nc).is_mine or game.get_cell(nr, nc).is_flagged
        )
        inner_unknown = sum(
            1 for nr, nc in inner_neighbors
            if not game.get_cell(nr, nc).is_revealed and not game.get_cell(nr, nc).is_flagged
        )

        config = game.get_config()
        total_mines = config.mine_count
        total_cells = config.rows * config.cols
        flagged_total = sum(
            1 for rr in range(config.rows) for cc in range(config.cols)
            if game.get_cell(rr, cc).is_flagged
        )
        revealed_total = sum(
            1 for rr in range(config.rows) for cc in range(config.cols)
            if game.get_cell(rr, cc).is_revealed
        )
        remaining_mines = total_mines - flagged_total
        remaining_unknown = total_cells - revealed_total - flagged_total
        base_prob = remaining_mines / remaining_unknown if remaining_unknown > 0 else 0.0

        estimated_outer = outer_known_mines + base_prob * outer_unknown
        estimated_inner_mines = raw + estimated_outer
        clamped = max(inner_known_mines, min(inner_unknown + inner_known_mines, round(estimated_inner_mines)))
        return clamped
assumptions: cell.adjacent_mines stores the raw differential value (inner - outer) as an integer, which this agent decodes back to an approximate inner mine count for the standard PAFG constraint logic
When outer unknowns exist, a global mine density estimate is used to approximate outer mine count, which may be imprecise but still outperforms treating the raw differential as a standard clue

description: Divides the board into a 4x4 grid of zones that must be fully cleared left-to-right top-to-bottom in order, rewarding skilled players who systematically deduce each sector while random agents waste turns clicking locked zones and fail to build sequential progress.

pafg_llm_agent.name: ProgressiveZoneAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Biases frontier cell scoring and opening action to prioritize the current required zone (left-to-right, top-to-bottom), so the agent systematically clears zones in order instead of wasting guesses in locked regions.
assumptions: Zones with no unrevealed safe cells are considered cleared, matching the ProgressiveZoneWin logic.
Opening click targets the center of zone 0 (top-left zone) to start clearing the first required zone immediately.

description: Each revealed cell shows the mine count within a large 5×5 neighborhood (24 cells), forcing skilled solvers to triangulate mine positions by differencing overlapping large-area sums across the board, while random agents cannot exploit the broader but diluted signal — slightly fewer mines keeps the game winnable for the constraint solver.

pafg_llm_agent.name: Radius2MooreNeighborhoodAgent
pafg_llm_agent.description: Overrides neighbor_positions to use the full 5x5 radius-2 Moore neighborhood so that clue constraints are correctly interpreted against the 24-cell area each revealed cell actually covers.
assumptions: The game uses radius-2-moore neighborhood meaning each clue covers all 24 cells in a 5x5 box; overriding neighbor_positions ensures the constraint solver builds correct equations.
postprocess_prob_map recalculates off-frontier cell probabilities using remaining mine count to improve guessing when pure constraint propagation leaves unknowns.
